nodes.label: Weight-Space Linear Recurrent Neural Networks (WARP model)
nodes.author: Roussel Desmond Nzoyem, Nawid Keshtmand, Enrique Crespo Fernandez, Idriss Tsayem, Raul Santos-Rodriguez, David A.W. Barton, Tom Deakin

nodes.label: WARP: Weight-space Adaptive Recurrent Prediction
nodes.rationale: WARP uses an auxiliary MLP ('root network') as the hidden state; its weights theta_t evolve via linear recurrence theta_t = A*theta_{t-1} + B*Delta_x_t, driven by input differences rather than raw inputs (inspired by continuous-time RNN theory). Decoding is non-linear (MLP applied to coordinates), combining linear recurrence efficiency (parallel scan) with expressivity from non-linear decoding. Enables gradient-free test-time adaptation and in-context learning as the root network adapts to context via weight-space dynamics.

nodes.label: Neural Network Weights as RNN Hidden State
nodes.rationale: WARP parametrizes RNN hidden state as the flattened weights of an auxiliary neural network; this high-dimensional representation enables infinite-capacity memory and non-linear decoding while maintaining the hardware efficiency of linear recurrence. Self-decoding (theta_t decodes itself) significantly reduces parameter count.

hyperedges.label: Weight-space hidden state enables gradient-free adaptation
hyperedges.description: WARP's weight-space linear RNN unifies the fast weight programmer paradigm with weight-space learning: the auxiliary network's weights serve as the hidden state, updated via linear recurrence with input differences, enabling gradient-free test-time adaptation.
